To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 8066 and 8062 antibodies bind to both the pre-hair-pin intermediate and the six-helix-bundle conformations of gp41, with affinities that differ by 150- to 200-fold, and that the binding stoichiometry of both the neutralizing and non neutralizing antibodies to the gp41 six helix bundle is one six helix bundle to one antibody.

the binding of neutralization-competent and non-competent Fab antibodies to the pre-hair-pin intermediate and six-hex bundle of HIV-1 envelope protein gp41 correlates with the neutralization potency of the antibody.

the binding affinities of neutralizing and nonneutralizing antibodies are similar, that binding to the six helix bundle is not involved in neutralization, and that neutralization involves a continuum of binding states along the fusion process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a new series of antibodies, directed against the N-HR of HIV-1, which bind to the pre-hair-pin intermediate and the six-helix-bundle conformations of gp41.
the development of broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV-1 and the elucidation of their mechanism of action.
the development of broadly neutralizing antibodies directed against the N-HR of gp41 and with the elucidation of the mechanism of their neutralizing activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of the 8066 neutralizing antibody, and presumably other broadly neutralizing antibodies, to the pre-hair-pin intermediate state of gp 41 is the critical step in neutralization.
binding of the neutralizing 8066 antibody to the six-hex bundle is not sufficient to neutralize HIV-1.
the binding affinity of the 8066 and 8062 mini-antibody Fab's for the six helix bundle is not the sole determinant for the neutralizing activity of the 8062 mini antibody.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding affinity of a neutralizing antibody for a pre-hairpin mimetic is not a reliable predictor of its neutralization potency.
the neutralizing antibody binds to a pre-hairpin conformation of gp41, while the non-neutralizing antibody binds to the pre-hairpins and the six-helix bundles of gp41.

the 8066 and 8062 antibodies are both capable of neutralizing HIV-1, and that the 8062 antibody is a non-neutralizing antibody that can be used for the design of non-neutralizing antibodies with neutralizing properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of the neutralizing antibody is more sensitive to the structural context in which the N-HR is found than that of the non-neutralizing antibody.

the neutralizing activity of antibodies against gp41 does not correlate with their affinity for the pre-hair-pin intermediate state of the fusion protein, but rather with their ability to bind to the six-hex bundle.

the binding affinities and stoichiometries of the neutralizing and nonneutralizing antibodies to the pre-hairpinned gp41 ectodomain are not significantly different, but the affinities for the six-helix-bundle conformation are very different.
